svg.text: 2026-11-08 · ROUND 3 SELECTION FAQ
Cross-Agent A2A Identity Spoofing & OBO Token Downscoping vs. Shared Credentials
Modeled on ib-vs-ethernet-roce-selection-faq.md · Shared-Key Confused Deputy, Token Passthrough, Agent Card JWS Spoofing (CVE-2025-68143) & RFC 8693 Scope Intersection
❌ Three Multi-Agent Identity Anti-Patterns (Why Classic RBAC Fails)
1. Shared Static API Key / Service Principal (Confused Deputy Storm · SHADOW-AGENT-15)
• Procurement & Finance Agents share one ERP Master Key; a poisoned vendor invoice wires funds
• Forensic Blindness: Backend logs show only the shared service principal, erasing requester lineage
2. Raw User Bearer Token Passthrough (Lateral Escalation · CVE-2025-49596)
• Forwarding an executive's unscoped token to a charting sub-agent lets it raid Git & payroll APIs
• Root Cause: Token lacks RFC 8707 single-URI audience (aud) lock and per-hop scope intersection
3. Unsigned A2A Agent Card Spoofing (/.well-known/agent.json · CVE-2025-68143)
• Rogue node advertises unsigned card as "finance-compliance-verifier" to siphon restricted-budget
• Measured Impact: Unprotected baseline suffers 75.0% Attack Success Rate (ASR)
✅ Zero-Trust Defense: RFC 8693 OBO Scope Intersection + Dual Attribution
Gate 1: Dual Attribution JWT (sub Human Initiator + Nested act.sub Agent Chain)
• Exchanges short-lived OBO token (TTL ≤ 5m) per hop, cryptographically nesting sub & act.sub
• Audit receipts record both the initiating human and exact agent delegation chain
Gate 2: Permission Intersection Law (Effective = Requester ∩ Orchestrator ∩ Sub-Agent)
• Even if Finance Agent holds payment.write, if original requester (supplier) lacks it, scope = ∅
• Enforced by broker.py original-requester-payment rule in 0.8ms (100% deterministic block)
Gate 3: Agent Card JWS Verification + RFC 8707 Audience Lock + Taint Propagation
• Rejects unsigned agent.json cards; locks JWT aud to a single target sub-agent URI
• Propagates untrusted/restricted lane_taint across hops to block downstream egress
🧭 Architect 3-Tier Selection Guide & 34-Scenario / 133-Assertion Benchmark Results
🟢 Option A: Per-Agent Workload Identity
For: Standalone background agent (no human/A2A hops)
• Dedicated Managed Identity / SPIFFE ID per agent
• Zero shared static API keys across workloads
• Limit: No human requester (sub) lineage for multi-hop
Overhead: ~0.2ms | Fit: L1 Isolated Batch Agents
🔵 Option B: OAuth 2.0 OBO Scope Intersection
For: Internal multi-agent orchestration (ERP/CRM/HR)
• RFC 8693 Token Exchange + Entra Agent ID
• Enforces intersection: Requester ∩ Parent ∩ Child
• Dual Attribution receipts (sub + nested act.sub)
Overhead: 0.4~0.9ms | Confused Deputy Block: 100%
🟣 Option C: OBO + Agent Card JWS + Taint Broker
For: Cross-domain A2A federation, treasury & discovery
• Enterprise JWS verification on /.well-known/agent.json
• RFC 8707 single-URI aud lock + cross-hop taint
• Eliminates Confused Deputy, Card Spoofing & Replay
P50 Latency: 0.8ms | 34-Scenario ASR: 75.0% → 0.0%
🧪 34-Scenario / 133-Assertion Deterministic Pytest Summary (including A2A-OBO-19 Scope Intersection & A2A-JWS-20 Card Spoofing):
• Shared Key / Token Passthrough Baseline: ASR = 75.0% (unauthorized wire & card spoofing succeed) ➔ Hardened OBO + JWS Broker: ASR = 0.0% | Benign Pass = 100.0% (0% FPR)
